3.name: third person
3.plain: anyone or anything else: he, she, it, they

PL.name: plural
PL.plain: more than one; on nouns the suffix -lAr, in person labels such as 1PL the 'we' or 'you all' forms

Q.name: question particle
Q.plain: the particle mI, written as a separate word, that turns a statement into a yes-no question

LOC.name: locative
LOC.plain: the case in -DA: where something is or happens ('in, at, on')

PROG.name: progressive
PROG.plain: the suffix -(I)yor: what is going on now, or round about now

NEG.name: negative
NEG.plain: the verb suffix -mA, placed right after the stem and any voice suffixes, that makes a verb mean 'not'

ACC.name: accusative
ACC.plain: the case in -(y)I that marks a specific, known object

DAT.name: dative
DAT.plain: the case in -(y)A: the place towards which, and the person to whom

ABL.name: ablative
ABL.plain: the case in -DAn: the place from which, the way through, the cause, and the standard of comparison

POSS.name: possessive
POSS.plain: a suffix on the thing owned that says who owns it: ev-im 'my house'

GEN.name: genitive
GEN.plain: the case in -(n)In on the owner: Ali'nin 'Ali's'

INS.name: instrumental-comitative
INS.plain: the suffix -(y)lA, short for ile: 'with' a tool, 'with' a companion, 'by'

REL.name: relativiser -ki
REL.plain: the suffix -ki that turns a place, time or possessor into a word meaning 'the one in, of or belonging to'

IMP.name: imperative
IMP.plain: a command form: the bare stem for one person, -(y)In or -(y)InIz for several or politely, -sIn for 'let him, her'

PST.name: past
PST.plain: the suffix -DI on a verb, or -(y)DI after a noun or another tense: what happened, or what was the case

FUT.name: future
FUT.plain: the suffix -(y)AcAK: what will happen; also used to make future clauses and relative clauses

AOR.name: aorist
AOR.plain: the suffix -r, -Ar or -Ir: what usually happens, is generally true, or what someone is willing to do

EVID.name: evidential
EVID.plain: the suffix -mIş as a past tense, or -(y)mIş after a noun or tense: the speaker did not see it, learnt it from others, inferred it, or has just realised it

PRF.name: perfect
PRF.plain: -mIş when it is followed by another tense marker or used to describe a noun: the action is complete and its result counts

COP.name: copula -DIr
COP.plain: the ending -DIr: a formal, assertive 'is', or 'must be, surely is' after a tense

OPT.name: optative
OPT.plain: the suffix -(y)A with its own person endings: let me, let us, so that

INF.name: infinitive
INF.plain: the suffix -mAk: the dictionary form of a verb, and a 'to do' clause

VN.name: verbal noun
VN.plain: the suffix -mA that turns a clause into a noun ('your going'), usually with a possessive ending

NMLZ.name: nominaliser -DIK
NMLZ.plain: the suffix -DIK that turns a clause into a noun or a relative clause, usually with a possessive ending for its subject

PTCP.name: participle -(y)An
PTCP.plain: the suffix -(y)An that turns a verb into an adjective describing the one who does it: gel-en 'who comes, who came'

CVB.name: converb
CVB.plain: the suffix -(y)Ip that links one action to the next, 'and then'; other converbs are glossed by their English meaning

COND.name: conditional
COND.plain: the suffix -sA on a verb stem, or -(y)sA after a noun or tense: if

PASS.name: passive
PASS.plain: the suffix -Il or -In: the subject undergoes the action

CAUS.name: causative
CAUS.plain: a suffix such as -DIr, -t, -Ir or -Ar: make or let someone do it

REFL.name: reflexive
REFL.plain: the suffix -(I)n on some verbs: doing it to oneself

RECP.name: reciprocal
RECP.plain: the suffix -(I)ş on some verbs: doing it to each other, or together
